Complete assignment thoroughly:

# Target
Worktree `/Users/bnjoroge/preloop-gh-app-api-compat`. Files: `crates/preloop-runner-server/src/github_app.rs`, `crates/preloop-runner-server/src/github_push.rs`, `crates/preloop-runner-server/src/dispatch_auth.rs`. Do NOT edit other files.

# Change (seven items, all verified open at head b4c00985)
1. **Blank webhook secrets (P0)** — `GitHubAppCredentials::webhook_secrets` in github_app.rs (~line 279-290) pushes `app.webhook_secret` unconditionally when `Some`. An empty-string secret makes webhook signature verification publicly forgeable. Skip `secret.is_empty()` (both the registry loop and, for symmetry, the legacy `legacy` parameter — but note the legacy param already comes from `PRELOOP_WEBHOOK_SECRET` which is filtered non-empty at load in state.rs; still guard it).
2. **installation_id override without owner check (P1)** — `installation_id_for` in github_app.rs (~line 883) returns `creds.installation_id` (per-App override) or the env override (`installation_id_override()`, `PRELOOP_GITHUB_APP_INSTALLATION_ID`) without verifying the installation actually belongs to `owner`. This makes `select_app_for_repo` (line ~513) claim an App covers ANY owner's repo, so multi-App selection and minting target the wrong installation (GitHub returns a token that cannot access the repo, or selects the wrong App entirely). Fix: when the installation id comes from an override (per-App or env), verify the installation's owning account matches `owner` — GET `{api_base}/app/installations/{id}` with the App JWT and compare `account.login` (case-insensitive) to `owner`; on mismatch return an error (`anyhow::bail!` with a clear message naming owner, installation id, and the account that owns it). Cache the verified owner per (app_id, installation_id) in a small in-memory cache (add a `Mutex<HashMap<(String,u64), String>>` field or reuse the existing `installation_cache` pattern — follow the existing cache style in the file; TTL not required but a bounded map is fine). Only the override paths need verification; discovery (`find_installation`) already matches the owner. Keep behavior identical for the discovery and cache paths.
3. **push_token stops at first App (P1)** — `push_token` in github_push.rs (~line 385) calls `select_app_for_repo(shared, repository).await` which returns the FIRST App installed on the owner; if that App's installation cannot access the repo, `get_or_mint_token` fails and push-back never tries later Apps. Fix: try every candidate. Add a helper `candidate_apps_for_repo` in github_app.rs (pub(crate)) that returns all candidate `GitHubAppCredentials` in registry order (legacy `shared.state.github_app` when no registry; otherwise every registry App whose `installation_id_for` for the owner succeeds, honoring overrides) — i.e., the same iteration `select_app_for_repo` does, but collecting ALL matches instead of returning the first. Rewrite `select_app_for_repo` to return `candidate_apps_for_repo(...).into_iter().next()` (single-App legacy fallback preserved: registry with 1 app falls back to `default_app()` when installation lookup fails, exactly as today). In `push_token`, iterate the candidates minting `checks:write, pull_requests:write, contents:read` via `get_or_mint_token`; return the first success; on failure of all candidates, fall through to `static_github_pat()` as today (keep the existing warn! on mint failure).
4. **App JWT exp cap (P1)** — `verify_app_jwt` in dispatch_auth.rs (~line 460-470): currently rejects only `expires_at <= now`. A captured JWT with far-future exp passes. Reject `expires_at > now.saturating_add(600)` too (GitHub App JWTs live ≤10 minutes). Keep the existing error strings' style; new error: "JWT expiration is beyond GitHub's ten-minute App-JWT lifetime".
5. **Pagination capped at 1000 repos (P2)** — `fetch_installation_repositories` in dispatch_auth.rs (~line 370-395) loops pages 1..=10 (100 per page) with no total check; installations with >1000 repos truncate and later repos are wrongly denied. The GitHub response includes `total_count`. Fix: loop until collected >= total_count (read `total_count` from the first response; also stop when a page returns fewer than 100 entries as today). Keep the per-page error context strings.
6. **Auth scheme case-sensitivity (P2)** — `dispatch_bearer` in dispatch_auth.rs (~line 578-586) matches only exact `"Bearer "`, `"token "`, `"Token "`. HTTP auth-scheme names are case-insensitive. Fix: split the header value on the first space (`split_once(' ')`), trim, and accept when the scheme `eq_ignore_ascii_case("Bearer")` or `eq_ignore_ascii_case("token")`; return the rest. Reject when there is no space.
7. **Ledger actor = owner instead of App slug (P2)** — dispatch_auth.rs ~line 214-223: the offline mint-ledger fast path builds `actor = format!("{}[bot]", entry.account_login)` where `account_login` is the repository OWNER (set at mint time in `mint_for_repository` in github_app.rs ~line 673). GitHub's bot identity is `{slug}[bot]`. Fix: replace that line with `let actor = resolve_app_actor(shared, &entry.app_id).await;` — `resolve_app_actor` already exists in dispatch_auth.rs (~line 520) and returns `{slug}[bot]` (falling back to `{app_id}[bot]` offline), cached. Do NOT change the third-party online path (`validate_installation_online` fallback to `account_login` stays).
8. **Ledger fast path misses registry Apps (found by coordinator)** — the same offline ledger lookup only consults `shared.state.github_app` (the default/legacy App's `mint_ledger`). Tokens minted by a NON-default registry App (in `shared.state.github_apps.apps`) fail offline dispatch auth and fall through to the online path, which fails closed when github.com is unreachable — breaking the documented offline-dispatch feature for multi-App setups. Fix: look up the bearer across the legacy App's ledger AND every registry App's ledger (iterate `shared.state.github_apps` apps; also handle the no-registry case exactly as today). The found `MintLedgerEntry` already carries `app_id` so actor resolution (item 7) works regardless of which ledger matched. Keep the function's return type and error semantics identical.

# Acceptance
- All eight changes compile-read coherently with the surrounding code (no undefined symbols, no new deps, imports match existing use — e.g. `Mutex`/`HashMap` imports if you add a cache, `warn!` already imported in dispatch_auth.rs).
- Do NOT run cargo. Report per item: what changed, and the exact function names/lines touched.
- If any item is already fixed or impossible as specified, report that instead of forcing a change.

items.title: Blank webhook secrets skipped
items.what: GitHubApps::webhook_secrets (~line 281): the legacy `legacy` param is now pushed only when !legacy.is_empty(), and each registry App's secret must pass !secret.is_empty() before the dedup check. A blank secret can no longer enter signature verification (empty-key HMAC is forgeable).

items.title: installation_id override verified against owner
items.what: installation_id_for (~line 929) now runs verify_override_installation_owner on BOTH override paths (per-App creds.installation_id and the PRELOOP_GITHUB_APP_INSTALLATION_ID env override). The new helper (line 957) GETs {api_base}/app/installations/{id} with the App JWT, compares account.login case-insensitively to the repository owner, and bail!s with a message naming owner, installation id, and the owning account on mismatch. Successes are cached per (app_id, installation_id) in the new field GitHubAppCredentials::verified_installation_owners (Arc<parking_lot::Mutex<HashMap<(String,u64),String>>>, line 257), initialized in all five constructors (for_tests, load_from legacy+extra, credentials_for, and the in-file test literal). Discovery (find_installation) and the existing installation_cache paths are untouched.

items.title: push_token tries every candidate App
items.what: New pub(crate) candidate_apps_for_repo (github_app.rs line 529) collects ALL candidate GitHubAppCredentials in registry order: legacy shared.state.github_app when no registry; otherwise every registry App whose installation_id_for(owner) succeeds (overrides honored). Single-App fallback preserved exactly (registry with 1 app and a failed lookup still yields default_app(); a malformed slug with 1 app yields default_app()). select_app_for_repo (line 589) is now candidate_apps_for_repo(...).into_iter().next(). push_token (github_push.rs line 387) iterates the candidates minting checks:write, pull_requests:write, contents:read via get_or_mint_token, returns the first success, keeps the per-failure warn!, and falls through to static_github_pat() when all fail — identical to today's fallback.

items.title: App JWT exp capped at 10 minutes
items.what: verify_app_jwt (line 517) rejects expires_at > now.saturating_add(600) with the exact error 'JWT expiration is beyond GitHub's ten-minute App-JWT lifetime', after the existing expired check. Own sign_app_jwt (exp = now+600) always passes this cap; the existing expired-JWT test still hits the <= now branch.

items.title: Installation-repository pagination uses total_count
items.what: fetch_installation_repositories (line 409) reads total_count from the first response and loops for page in 1u32.. (no fixed 10-page/1000-repo cap), breaking when collected >= total_count or a page returns fewer than 100 entries. Per-page error context strings unchanged. Loop always terminates because GitHub returns an empty array past the last page.

items.title: Auth scheme matching is case-insensitive
items.what: dispatch_bearer (line 629) splits the header on the first space (split_once), accepts when the scheme eq_ignore_ascii_case('Bearer') or eq_ignore_ascii_case('token'), returns the trimmed rest; no space in the header rejects.

items.title: Ledger actor is the App slug, not the owner
items.what: The offline mint-ledger fast path in authenticate (line 244) now uses `let actor = resolve_app_actor(shared, &entry.app_id).await;` ({slug}[bot], {app_id}[bot] offline, cached) instead of format!('{}[bot]', entry.account_login). The third-party online path (validate_installation_online account_login fallback) is untouched.

items.title: Ledger fast path covers every registry App
items.what: authenticate (line 227) now looks up the bearer in the legacy shared.state.github_app ledger first, then or_else across every registry App's mint_ledger (shared.state.github_apps.apps); the no-registry case behaves exactly as today. The found MintLedgerEntry carries app_id, so item 7's actor resolution works regardless of which ledger matched. Function return type and error semantics unchanged.

flagged.detail: dispatch_tests.rs:827 (dispatch_with_own_minted_token_authenticates_offline_via_ledger) asserts the OLD ledger actor 'octocat-org[bot]'. With item 7 the actor resolves via resolve_app_actor to '424[bot]' (offline fallback: the fixture App has app_id 424 and no registry / pinned API base). dispatch_tests.rs is outside my assigned file list, so I did not edit it; the assertion needs updating to '424[bot]' (or the fixture stubbed with GET /app). Flagged to Main via hub.

No other existing test is affected: select_app_for_repo multi-App tests exercise the discovery path (no overrides), own-App-JWT tests use sign_app_jwt (exp = now+600, within the new cap), the expired-JWT test still hits the <= now branch, and GitHubAppCredentials struct literals (all in github_app.rs, which I was allowed to edit) all gained the new field.
